item.title: Cockroach Party
item.content:encoded:
Hi! Draft is available under the "Cockroach Party" tab. It's about… um… cockroaches. And thaumaturgy. Idea was obtained from the Random SCP Concept Generator: "Cockroaches that must be fed magic."

http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/oystershell

Specific points of critique I'm looking for help with:

Is there an existing designation for individuals who can sense thaumaturgic activity?

Is the description expressed clearly enough to follow? If not, how to proceed

Any suggestions for the refinement of the test logs to make them funnier or squickier or more bizarre etc.

Does the pacing work? I attempted to integrate a humor->mild horror->humor progression. If it does not work, how to proceed.

Would the article benefit from Nowak being connected to Serpent's Hand? I decided to err on the side of simplicity and left it out of this draft, but if it's a funny idea I'll add it back in.

Thanks for your time!

item.title: Tale: Like a Hole in the Head
item.description: Cybersecurity, Human Error, PTSD and Swiss Cheese
item.content:encoded:
http://scpsandbox2.wikidot.com/eads

Hi, I've wrote up my first Tale. It's in the first tab on my sandbox page. It's Pretty Long, and would be the start to a bit of a longer series (probably three parts?). I featured two not-terribly popular Series III SCiPs, my 2918 and RecursiveRecursion's 2789.

Derek Kato was involved in a prior incident that led to the containment of SCP-2918 and amnesticized. Scouted by an old military buddy, he goes through an unorthodox "interview" process to be recruited as a field agent. Along the way, a series of coincidences preclude the proper channels from recognizing that he should be barred from being recruited. Similarly, a little set of internal coincidences lead him to actually accept.

I haven't been active in a while and the Greenlight Policy is new to me. As far as I understand, if I already have surviving mainlist articles, I don't need Greenlights to draft a Tale, right?

I'm going to PM the author of 2789, but as a general question I didn't happen to spot anywhere in the FAQs: Is it impolite to write someone else's work into a Tale without asking? Edit: Got these questions answered on the IRC.

item.title: Tale - MTF Agents Investigate An Anomaly
item.description: A mystery that unfolds into an unorthodox heist story.
item.content:encoded:
Post)

Link to sandbox

Here is a draft for a Tale about a couple of MTF Field Agents working a case. They will follow a trail of clues that ultimately unravels into a grand caper.

This is the first part of a larger story, but it will probably be posted in segments, so this is the first installment. For now just needing crit on the part up until End Act 1 before the Working Notes.

The story takes place in a city during a sanitation workers strike, so there is uncollected garbage everywhere. The anomaly in question involves sapient trucks that are going around and "stealing" this trash, but there will be a couple twists before the Crew's true motive comes to light by the end.

Here is a link to an Ideas Forum thread where the big picture plot is explained in more detail.

At this stage we are mainly looking for a line-by-line on spots where issues like grammar and punctuation might be noticeably bad, but any other feedback or opinions are welcome too. Thanks!

item.title: The Click
item.description: Do you ever just click with someone?
item.content:encoded:
http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/oystershell

Draft is available under "The Click" tab.

I feel kind of bad posting this while my other draft is up for critique, but the rules say I can, so I'm going for it. I had the idea for this skip this morning and spent all day today writing it in a haze. I've proofread, but errors are likely. Let me know!

Specific points of critique I'm looking for help with:

Dialogue. It's not my strong suit and there's a lot of it. Does it work? Does it resonate emotionally? If not, how to proceed.

Should the very end be removed? I feel like the final monologue could be stupid and/or too revelatory. If so, how to proceed.

Thanks for your time.

EDIT: This draft is in rewrite and does not require critique at this time.
